sentences.text: 1. Heard learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu A. Jha appearing for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Aditya Davda appearing for the respondent - State and learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw appearing for the respondent Nos.2 and 3 - Corporation.

2. With the consent of learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, the matter was taken up finally.
Hence, RULE.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Aditya Davda waives the service of rule on behalf of the respondent No.1 - State and learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw waives the service of rule on behalf of the respondents No.2 and 3.
3.
At the outset, learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha tendered a further affidavit across the bar which is affirmed by the petitioner on 11.3.2025.
The affidavit is taken on record.

4. By way of this petition, the petitioner has prayed for quashing and setting aside the order dated 21.12.2021 passed by the respondent No.3 at Annexure - A to the petition and has further prayed to hold and declare the petitioner eligible and entitled to be appointed as driver in respondent No.2 Corporation and as per the prayer made in paragraph No.9E, the petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined has prayed for a more specific direction to appoint him on the post of Driver in respondent No.3 Amreli Division.
5.

Brief facts of the petition can be summarized as under :-
5.1

That the respondent No.2 issued an advertisement for recruitment to the post of Driver by way of an advertisement No. GSRTC/201920/1 dated 09.10.2019 and as the petitioner was meeting with the required qualification, he applied for the same and thereafter, he was called for testing his efficiency in driving skill on 14.10.2019 and ultimately was declared successful.
Thereafter, a select list was prepared wherein the petitioner was at serial No. 50 and he was called for selection of place / posting on 8.10.2021.
The petitioner remained present in the said camp and had chosen Amreli District as a preferred district.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined vide communication dated 12.10.2021 asked the petitioner to submit No Objection Certificate from the Medical Officer and Police Officer within three days of issuance of final appointment order.
According to the petition, the petitioner submitted Medical Certificate as per the requirement.

Though nothing is stated in the petition about No Objection Certificate by the Police Department,
learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha drew attention of this Court to a Certificate issued by Police Inspector, Amreli Rural Police Station dated 26.10.2021 indicating that there are two offences registered against the petitioner in Amreli Rural Police Station, one offence was pending which was registered at Savarkundla Police Station and in one of the offence registered at Amreli Rural Police Station, in two offences petitioner is acquitted.

As per the petition and as per the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined facts stated by learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha, at page No.52,
it is pointed out by learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha that it is not a part of the petition or averment made by learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha but that has come on record by way of affidavit in reply by the respondent - Corporation.

Aforesaid facts are concealed by the petitioner about registration of other offences which the Court has found on page No.52 in the Certificate and in the petition after referring to Medical Certificate in paragraph No.3 and 4, the petitioner has straightway jumped to an offence registered before Savarkundla Police Station on 20.8.2020 under Section 498A, 323, 325 and 114 of Indian Penal Code.

According to the petitioner, it was the case filed by the wife of the petitioner by way of an FIR against all family members of the petitioner including the petitioner and therefore, according to the petitioner, the respondent No.3 vide order dated 21.12.2021 rejected the case of the petitioner for NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined appointment on the ground of registration of FIR against the petitioner and that is how the above action and order dated 21.12.2021 is challenged by way of this petition by the petitioner.
6. Learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha in view of above facts made following submissions :-
6.1 According to learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha the concealment about the fact that FIRs are registered against the petitioner was not willful and deliberate.

According to learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha now the petitioner has been acquitted in respect of all the offences and therefore, as now nothing has remained against the petitioner, his case is required to be considered for appointment which the petitioner has cleared and found his name at serial No.50 in the select list and the appointment is denied to the petitioner only on account of pendency of criminal case at the relevant point of time vide order dated 21.12.2021.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined 6.2
According to learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha the petitioner had no knowledge about the fact that he will have to disclose the facts about registration of every single FIR registered against him.
He submitted that in view of acquittal of the petitioner in all the cases even now those details have become insignificant for denying the appointment to the petitioner.

As far as suppression is concerned, learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha submitted that at the relevant point of time when the petition was filed, (not at the time when Form was filed) out of five FIRs, only the FIR registered with Savarkundla Police Station on 20.08.2020 under Section 498, 323, 325 and 114 of Indian Penal Code was pending trial.

Pursuant to the said FIR, the trial had already completed and was kept for judgment and the judgment was delivered on 25.2.2022 and in respect of the rest of the FIRs, at the time of filing of the petition, the petitioner was already acquitted NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined and therefore, the petitioner did not think it appropriate to mention about the FIR pursuant to which the petitioner was already acquitted at the time of filing of the petition.

6.3 Learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha relied upon a decision of High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in case of Mandeep Kaur Versus Canara Bank and another in CWP 1827 of 2019 decided on 31.10.2022 and by relying upon the aforesaid decision submitted that as per the view taken by the Punjab and Haryana High Court,

Thereafter, he relied upon another decision of Allahabad High Court in case of Harendra Panwar Versus State of U.P. and Others in Writ Appeal No. 51247 of 2007 decided on 16.2.2012 and by relying upon the aforesaid decision, he submitted that merely because some vital information is concealed or withheld by the petitioner, that would not dis-entitle him from NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined opting for the job.

sentences.text: By relying upon aforesaid two decisions, learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha submitted that merely because the petitioner did not disclose about registration of FIR, the respondents were not justified in rejecting the petitioner's candidature and not appointing him on the post of driver only on account of concealment of facts related to registration of FIR.
He, therefore, prayed for allowing the petition and to direct the respondents to appoint the petitioner on the post of driver in respondent No. 3 Amreli Division.

7. Except for above submissions, no other submissions were made by learned advocate Mr.
Sudhanshu Jha appearing for the petitioner.

8. Learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw appearing for the S T Corporation vehemently opposed the petition and submitted that the application form had a specific column just before the undertaking and signature wherein every applicant has to state the facts in YES or NO in NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined respect of a question which reads as under :-
"Whether any offence under IPC has been registered or any case is pending before any Police Authority or Criminal Court?" and the petitioner was required to answer the above question only in YES or NO.

When the petitioner had not disclosed the correct facts and despite the fact that there were at least four offences registered against the petitioner at the time when the form was filled up by the petitioner, such concealment would show the dishonest intention of the petitioner and any candidate who applies for a job is expected to be honest enough to disclose all relevant facts related to his character.
9. If a person conceals the fact about registration of an offence that itself shows that his intentions were dishonest.

Intensity or gravity of offence and to what extent even despite having such offence registered against the petitioner whether he can be appointed or not is a question which can be determined only on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined basis of nature of offence.

For a petty offence, the organization looking to the nature of offence may take a decision to appoint a candidate despite registration of offence and subject to final outcome of the trial but if nature of offence is grave, the organization may choose to wait till the final outcome of the trial.
Everything depends upon the nature of offence but for that, first the candidate must show the courage to face the reality and to state everything with utmost honesty to the recruiting authority.

In absence of showing courage to put forward everything about the characteristic of a person in black and white, before the authority by filing up the application form correctly, a persons overall characteristic cannot be decided nor the organization will get a correct picture about the overall characteristic of a person.

The forms was to be filled up in vernacular language only i.e. Gujarati and all that the petitioner was to disclose was only the fact NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/03/2025 undefined about whether any case is registered against him under Indian Penal Code or whether any case against the petitioner is pending before any Court or Police Authority.

11. What is important is the intention of a candidate at the threshold while filling up the form and not the outcome of the criminal case because unless a person honestly discloses about registration of offence, no further inquiry would be possible for the recruiting body to have any knowledge about the nature of offence and despite having such case registered against the petitioner, to what extent such registration of case can be overlooked and a candidate can be appointed.

Therefore, learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw submitted that at the time of filing of the form, it is the intention of the petitioner that is required to be seen and not the nature of offence and its gravity and to what extent it can have any positive or adverse impact over the petitioner's appointment is something which can be assessed only if the petitioner honestly NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022
JUDGMENT
DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined states about the nature of offence and provide the details about the same

In the instant case, the petitioner had remained silent all throughout about registration of offence and therefore, that shows the dishonest intention on the part of the petitioner to secure the job by hook or crook even by concealing such vital information from the recruiting body and therefore, such act cannot be pardoned and such deliberate attempt on the part of petitioner to secure the appointment by dishonest means of concealing vital facts about registration of not one but four offences against him in past is required to be considered and therefore, the petition is required to be dismissed with heavy costs.

12.1 Learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw drew attention of the Court that in respect of judgment in case of Mandeep Kaur Versus Canara Bank and another (Supra) relied upon by the petitioner, the FIR was registered against the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined petitioner after joining the training i.e. after the petitioner was selected and thereafter a criminal case was registered against the petitioner and therefore, the question about concealment or dishonest intention was not examined by the Court and therefore, at the relevant point of time what was considered by the Court was whether registration of such FIR against the petitioner would disqualify him for the job merely because FIR is registered and therefore, according to learned advocate Mr. Munshaw, the ratio of the decision relied upon by learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha in case of Mandeep Kaur Versus Canara Bank and another (Supra) would not apply in the facts of the case.
12.2

However, it was pointed out by learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw that by the time, the aforesaid fact had come into knowledge of the authority and petitioner's appointment was cancelled,
he was already appointed and posted in the department and in view of the fact that some equity was Rameshbhai Danabhai Khetariya vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92013975/

, the case of the petitioner was considered in light of equity having been created in favour of the petitioner.

12.3 In the instant case, the respondents have received the information about registration of four criminal cases against the petitioner well within time and even the appointment order itself is not issued and therefore, no equity is created in favour of the petitioner and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined therefore, the respondent - Corporation is well within its right to discard a dishonest candidate from the selection procedure who has never thought it fit to bring it to the notice of the recruiting authority that there are not just one or two but as many as four criminal cases registered against him.

Learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw therefore submitted that when the application form is required to be filled up by the candidate, one of the purpose behind filing up the form and asking for certain details about the registration of offence and other relevant aspects is to determine the character of a candidate and when the petitioner had not even furnished the correct details about registration of an offence, such person with dishonest intention is definitely unfit for offering him a job irrespective of outcome of criminal case and therefore, according to learned advocate Mr.
H. S. Munshaw, present petition is required to be dismissed with heavy costs.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined 13.
I have heard learned advocates appearing for the parties and perused the record.

Upon perusal of record, I found that the petitioner had produced the form which was filled up by the petitioner on 13.07.2019 at 20:29 as can been seen from the bottom of the form filled up by the petitioner.
The form bears the signature of the present petitioner and apart from other usual information just before undertaking which is just at the bottom of form, every candidate has to give an undertaking.

Translation of the undertaking given by the petitioner reads as under :-
(Translated Version) "I, RAMESHBHAI DANABHAI KHETARIYA rightfully declare that the above information true to my knowledge.

If any of the information provided herein above is found to be false or incorrect or if any incorrect information is furnished on the basis of any certificate in that case the decision of the Corporation would be final and the same would be binding upon me.
Further, I have not been NEUTRAL CITATION C/
JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined convicted by any of the Criminal Court

and I assure that there is no complaint or case pending against me before any Police Authority or Criminal Court."
Just above the undertaking, the candidate has to state in Yes or No and answer the following question : "Any offence under IPC has been registered ? Or Any Case /
Complaint is pending before any of the Police Authority / Criminal Court ?"

Against this question which is asked in vernacular language in the application form, the petitioner has in vernacular language replied NO.
14.

Today, learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha has filed further affidavit and tried to elaborately explain that it was a mistake on the part of the petitioner and that the petitioner tried to fill the form in the local cyber cafe at Amreli and it was not a deliberate mistake, he was not expert in operating computer and therefore, he did not fill up the form.
The petitioner has come up with all these excuses after filing the petition and after six years NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022

sentences.text: 15. It is true that the cases against the petitioners have resulted into acquittal but what is more important is the conduct of the petitioner.
The first case was registered against the petitioner in the year 2015 which was under Section 506(2) of Indian Penal Code and the same was registered as Criminal Case No. 1538 of 2015.
Of course, the said case was decided on 10.11.2017 and the petitioner was acquitted but the petitioner did not disclose about the aforesaid acquittal in the form.
He could have answered the above question in Yes and thereafter, could have furnished the details NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined about his acquittal.
However, the same is not the case with the other offences registered against the petitioner.

One more offence under Section 323 and 504 of Indian Penal Code and under Section 135 of Gujarat Police Act was registered against the petitioner for which Criminal Case No. 398 of 2017 was registered against the petitioner and the same was decided on 25.02.2012 i.e. after almost three years after the petitioner filled up the form and concealed the facts about registration of offence which was registered in the year 2017 i.e. two years prior to the date on which the petitioner filled up the form.
16.

Third FIR registered against the petitioner was on 12.01.2019 under Section 323 and 504 of Indian Penal Code and under Section 135 of Gujarat Police Act for which Criminal Case No.817 of 2019 was registered and the same was decided on 26.08.2019 and the petitioner was acquitted.

However, the date on which the form NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined was filled up by the petitioner, the petitioner was not acquitted, the case was pending and the petitioner did not disclose the aforesaid fact.

17. One more case was registered against the petitioner on 10.01.2020 under Section 337, 504,
506(2) and 114 of Indian Penal Code and under Section 135 of Gujarat Police Act for which Criminal Case No.376 of 2021 was registered and the same was decided on 04.01.2022 and the petitioner was acquitted.

18. The last case against the petitioner was registered on 27.07.2020 under Section 498(C),325, 323,
504 and 114 of Indian Penal Code for which Criminal Case No. 900 of 2020 was registered and the same was decided vide order dated 27.06.2023 whereby the petitioner was acquitted.

19. A perusal of above record related to criminal history or registration of FIR against the petitioner would indicate that even if the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/03/2025 undefined details about three offences, one registered in the year 2015 and the petitioner was acquitted in the year 2017 i.e. much prior to filling up the form and the last tow offences which were registered in the year 2020 i.e. after filling up the form are discarded then also on the date on which the petitioner filled up the form there were two criminal cases pending against the petitioner which the petitioner concealed while filing of the application form.

Therefore, the fact remains that at the time when the application form was filled up by the petitioner, irrespective of Rameshbhai Danabhai Khetariya vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92013975/
7 other cases wherein the petitioner was either acquitted prior to filling up the form or were registered subsequently, the petitioner had knowledge about registration of two FIRs registered against him on the date on which the form was filled up by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 20. Every recruiting body has a right to assess the character of a candidate who is willing to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined join the organization by passing the test for any employment and for every employer the quality of employee and his characteristic are one of the most important factors which any recruiting body would consider.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was opting for a job in a Semi Government Organization wherein usually all the salary, other packages and perks are considered to be better than the private sector and even the recruiting body being State, the rules for termination or imposing any punishment or even to initiate departmental proceedings are stringent, every recruiting body would expect the candidate to come with the clean hands and show utmost honesty and diligence because ultimately, if any wrong candidate is selected, the organization either will have to bear with him all throughout during his career or the organization would require to keep fighting legal battle to get rid of such dishonest person once having entered the organization, which would result into not just monetary loss to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined organization but sometime may affect the overall image also of the organization.

21. When we speak of maintaining the highest standard of honesty and integrity in every job, it becomes the duty of the candidates to show courage and to put forward every single facts which may go in his favour or against him before the recruiting body irrespective of its final outcome.
The test as to whether registration of offence would itself disqualify a person or not is a question that the organization is required to consider subsequently.

If a person shows courage to place the correct fact before the recruiting body about registration of offence, then only it is for the organization to consider that whether such pendency of criminal case or registration of offence is of such nature that it will disqualify a person from getting a job.

In the instant case, the petitioner has failed in climbing even the first step to show his honest intention by placing on record the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined correct facts about his past record.

When a person is found to be dishonest right from the inception, the organization was justified in denying him the appointment on the ground of pendency of criminal offence because the petitioner did not disclose the fact about pendency of criminal offence and any recruiting body is expected to consider the case of petitioner or candidate in light of gravity of offence, only if the candidate discloses the correct facts before the organization and not otherwise.

22. I have reasons to say so as today we are living in a high tech world and therefore, when an organization or recruiting body asked for a specific details from the candidate about any past offences registered against him or about any pending criminal cases, unless the candidate on his own provides the details, it would be very difficulty for the recruiting body or organization to dig out the past of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined candidate and to verify his credentials.

The certificate issued by a local police authority may give an idea about the cases registered or pending against the person who are within the jurisdiction or database collected by the concerned police authority but at the same time, suppose if Rameshbhai Danabhai Khetariya vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92013975/
8 a person, opt for a job in a particular District or State but has committed an offence or if the same is registered or pending with some other State in that case, despite the candidate having a criminal history or pending case, the same would never come to surface on the basis of certificate issued by the concerned police authority having limited jurisdiction and resources to examine and verify the same and therefore, it becomes the mandatory moral duty of the candidate to disclose about every single offence or pending case registered or instituted against him at the time of filling up the form to give a clear picture about his credibility to the recruiting body or the organization and

thereafter,
it is a matter of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined discretion or subject to any rules framed by the authority to consider candidature of the petitioner and to proceed further to give appointment to the candidate depending upon nature of offence, its gravity and depending upon the extent of candidate allegedly involved in the offence.

23. As far as the judgment relied upon by learned advocate Mr. Sudhanshu Jha in case of Mandeep Kaur Versus Canara Bank and another (Supra) is concerned as rightly pointed out by learned advocate Mr. H. S. Munshaw that after the petitioner was sent to training and he joined the training,
during the process of selection, a criminal case was registered and since in that case, it was not the case that deliberately the petitioner did not disclose the fact about registration of criminal case, the case was considered by the concerned Court by taking into consideration the gravity of offence and contents of FIR whereas here it is the case about the intention of the petitioner and to how NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined far he has remained honest while filling up the form.

As far as the second decision relied upon by the petitioner in case of Harendra Panwar Versus State of U.P. and others (Supra) is concerned, there also at the time when it was noted by the authority that petitioner has concealed the fact about registration of FIR against him, equity was created in favour of the petitioner and he was already offered a job whereas in the instant case, the respondents have acted well within time and even before petitioner could be offered job when the aforesaid facts were noted by the respondents, the respondents had passed the order dated 21.12.2021 and disqualified the petitioner from the job.

sentences.text: 25. In view of above, I don't see any error committed by the respondents in passing the order dated 21.12.2021.
Accordingly, present petition is required to be dismissed and the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined same is dismissed.

No order as to costs.

11. What is important is the intention of a candidate at the threshold while filling up the form and not the outcome of the criminal case because unless a person honestly discloses about registration of offence, no further inquiry would be possible for the recruiting body to have any knowledge about the nature of offence and despite having such case registered against the petitioner, to what extent such registration of case can be overlooked and a candidate can be appointed.
In the instant case, the petitioner had remained silent all throughout about registration of offence and therefore, that shows the dishonest intention on the part of the petitioner to secure the job by hook or crook even by concealing such vital information from the recruiting body and therefore, such act cannot be pardoned and such deliberate attempt on the part of petitioner to secure the appointment by dishonest means of concealing vital facts about registration of not one but four offences against him in past is required to be considered and therefore, the petition is required to be dismissed with heavy costs.
12.3 In the instant case, the respondents have received the information about registration of four criminal cases against the petitioner well within time and even the appointment order itself is not issued and therefore, no equity is created in favour of the petitioner and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined therefore, the respondent - Corporation is well within its right to discard a dishonest candidate from the selection procedure who has never thought it fit to bring it to the notice of the recruiting authority that there are not just one or two but as many as four criminal cases registered against him.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In absence of showing courage to put forward everything about the characteristic of a person in black and white, before the authority by filing up the application form correctly, a persons overall characteristic cannot be decided nor the organization will get a correct picture about the overall characteristic of a person.
The first case was registered against the petitioner in the year 2015 which was under Section 506(2) of Indian Penal Code and the same was registered as Criminal Case No. 1538 of 2015.

Every recruiting body has a right to assess the character of a candidate who is willing to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined join the organization by passing the test for any employment and for every employer the quality of employee and his characteristic are one of the most important factors which any recruiting body would consider.
Considering the fact that the petitioner was opting for a job in a Semi Government Organization wherein usually all the salary, other packages and perks are considered to be better than the private sector and even the recruiting body being State, the rules for termination or imposing any punishment or even to initiate departmental proceedings are stringent, every recruiting body would expect the candidate to come with the clean hands and show utmost honesty and diligence because ultimately, if any wrong candidate is selected, the organization either will have to bear with him all throughout during his career or the organization would require to keep fighting legal battle to get rid of such dishonest person once having entered the organization, which would result into not just monetary loss to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined organization but sometime may affect the overall image also of the organization.
21. When we speak of maintaining the highest standard of honesty and integrity in every job, it becomes the duty of the candidates to show courage and to put forward every single facts which may go in his favour or against him before the recruiting body irrespective of its final outcome.
The test as to whether registration of offence would itself disqualify a person or not is a question that the organization is required to consider subsequently.
If a person shows courage to place the correct fact before the recruiting body about registration of offence, then only it is for the organization to consider that whether such pendency of criminal case or registration of offence is of such nature that it will disqualify a person from getting a job.
In the instant case, the petitioner has failed in climbing even the first step to show his honest intention by placing on record the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/947/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined correct facts about his past record.
When a person is found to be dishonest right from the inception, the organization was justified in denying him the appointment on the ground of pendency of criminal offence because the petitioner did not disclose the fact about pendency of criminal offence and any recruiting body is expected to consider the case of petitioner or candidate in light of gravity of offence, only if the candidate discloses the correct facts before the organization and not otherwise.
